title: Toby and Maple's Ferry Fix
markdown:
Dawn broke. Not a sleepy dawn. A bright, bold dawn burst through Toby the raccoon’s window like a trumpet. Golden light tumbled onto his paws. He stretched, yawned wide, wiggled his whiskers. Today was THE day. Whispering Isle Orchard. His tummy did a flip-flop. Not just any day. An adventure day.

He dashed to the window, legs a blur. Dewdrops sparkled like a carpet of tiny diamonds. Birdsong burst from every tree, a tinkling that made him want to tap his feet. “It’s perfect!” He grabbed his trusty tool belt: sprockets, springs, a tiny wrench, and a particularly bendy bit of wire saved from a broken toy car.

He skittered out, bushy tail behind him. “Maple! Maple!” He could practically taste the crisp apples.

Maple the heron, perched still on a smooth grey stone, blinked her amber eyes. She tilted her long neck. “Good morning, Toby. You seem particularly… springy. Found a new bounce?”

“Bouncy is an understatement! The orchard! Ripe apples! And we’ll take the ferry! The quick way!”

Maple nodded slowly. “A splendid day for it. I checked the ferry yesterday. A quick peek.”

But at the rickety rope ferry, Toby’s bright eyes narrowed. Uh-oh. Whiskers drooped a fraction. The rope that held the ferry steady was floppy. Frayed. A fat knot had popped, leaving a gaping hole. The ferry sagged, more tired puddle than boat.

“Crikey! It’s broken!” Another flip-flop, worried this time. The sun was climbing, painting the sky cheerful. They needed to cross before it took its sleepy bow. Wait too long and they’d miss the best apples.

Maple peered, missing nothing. “The main mooring rope has snapped.” Her beak pointed to a frayed end dangling uselessly. “A bit of a pickle. A rather sticky situation.”

“A pickle? It’s a whole giant gherkin!” Toby rummaged wildly. He pulled out a coil of thick green twine he’d “borrowed” from a forgotten kite. He’d always known that kite string was good for something important. “We can fix this. We have to!”

Maple scanned bank and trees. “Something sturdy to secure it. Something that won’t snap. And something to grip the planks. The moss is slippery after last night’s dew.”

Toby’s brain whirred like a tiny determined engine. “You look for a strong tough vine! The kind that’s hard to break! I’ll tackle the wobbly bits and find extra grip!”

The adventure kicked into high gear. Maple, with incredible eyesight, spotted a thick twisting vine high on a sturdy willow, tough as old boots. She plucked a long section with her beak, like a colourful ribbon. Toby found a discarded splintery board that looked as if it had fallen off a boat. With clever twists of bendy wire and sturdy knots, he attached small rough pebbles to its underside. He yanked. “Perfect! For when the ferry tips or the planks get slippery!” He puffed his chest.

Back at the ferry he threaded the vine through the rickety frame, knotting with practiced skill, each knot tight, pulling with all his might. Maple’s long precise beak guided the rope through tricky holes and under loose planks. The sun beat warm on their backs. Toby’s fur felt a little too toasty. Sweat trickled. He tugged one last mighty knot.

“There!” He panted, wiping his brow. “Stronger than ever! That vine is tough stuff!”

Maple gave the repaired rope a gentle tug. It held. “Excellent work. A truly spectacular repair. Now, to the island!”

A mighty push sent the ferry bobbing out into the river. Toby grabbed a sturdy well-worn paddle. Maple, with a mighty beat of her wings, helped steer and keep the ferry balanced. The water rippled and splashed. Toby paddled with all his might, little arms working like pistons. His paws burned a little, but his eyes were fixed on the distant green shape of the island. The sun was a bright warm disc, sinking lower. Shadows stretched long across the water, turning the river a beautiful deep blue. Once the ferry listed; the pebble-board bit and held. Toby grinned at his own invention and nearly dropped the paddle.

“Faster, Toby! The sun waits for no one, not even raccoons and herons!”

He gritted his teeth and paddled harder. Push, pull, splash. The ferry bobbed and dipped like a little boat in a grand ocean. They were racing the golden descent. He imagined juicy apples, red skins gleaming. That thought spurred him.

Just as the last sliver of orange kissed the horizon, pink and purple streaks above, they bumped the sandy shore of Whispering Isle. The air smelled of sweet ripe apples. Toby’s tummy rumbled louder. Trees heavy with ruby-red and golden fruit reached toward twilight.

He grinned, face crinkling. “We made it!” He dropped the paddle with a clatter. “Just in time!”

Maple landed gracefully, long legs folding. “Just in time, my friend. A spectacular landing.”

They looked at the bounty, apples glowing softly. Toby’s tummy sang. The broken rope, the paddle-burn, the nick of time — that felt even better than the first bite. He pocketed a pebble that had done its job, and they began to pick, the ferry tied firm behind them, vine and kite-string holding as if they had always meant to.
